findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that all guards (cycle, closed-ticket, etc.) are evaluated as a pre-flight check *before* the unlink is issued for mis-escalated repairs, so that an edge is only unlinked when the replacement write is known to succeed (or define a compensating re-link on add_dependency failure).
evidence: 'Repair unlinks the recorded edge and writes the re-resolved one'

'--repair on an edge whose re-resolution would create a cycle reports the edge as unrepairable and leaves it in place, rather than raising out of the command' — this implies cycle detection happens in the failure test, but the plan does not specify that the cycle check (and all other guards) are evaluated BEFORE the unlink is committed
ABSENCE: no mention of pre-flight validation before destructive unlink, nor rollback/compensating write if add_dependency subsequently rejects the pair
findings.finding: For mis-escalated repair, the plan sequences two non-atomic writes: unlink the old edge, then write the re-resolved edge via add_dependency. If add_dependency fails after unlink has already succeeded (e.g., the re-resolved pair triggers a cycle guard or closed-ticket guard that was not caught in pre-flight), the store is left with neither the old edge nor the new one — a silent partial-write data loss.
findings.location: Approach section — 'Repair reuses the existing add_dependency and unlink write paths'
scenarios: A mis-escalated edge is being repaired; re-resolution yields a pair where one ticket was closed between scan time and repair time; unlink fires, add_dependency rejects with closed-ticket guard, edge is permanently gone with no record of the original pair.
Race: user closes a ticket between dry-run preview and actual --repair execution; same partial-write outcome.
findings.suggested_fix: In link_audit.py, for each mis-escalated repair: (1) call a dry-run or validation pass of add_dependency on the re-resolved pair first; (2) only if it passes, call unlink then add_dependency; (3) if add_dependency unexpectedly fails after unlink, immediately re-issue the original unlink as an add_dependency with the original pair and log a WARNING. Document this ordering in the plan's Approach section.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that for `mis-escalated` repair the relink attempt is validated (or attempted) BEFORE the unlink is committed, or otherwise document how partial failure (unlink succeeds, relink fails for a non-cycle reason such as a closed-ticket guard) is detected and recovered; add a corresponding test case.
evidence: Plan: 'Repair unlinks the recorded edge and writes the re-resolved one.'

ABSENCE: no ordering constraint stated — plan does not specify whether unlink or relink executes first, or whether the unlink is suppressed until the relink is confirmed safe.
findings.finding: The repair path for `mis-escalated` edges is a non-atomic two-step (unlink the old edge, then write the re-resolved edge). The plan only names the cycle-guard failure path as 'unrepairable and left in place,' but does not address partial failure where the UNLINK event commits successfully and the subsequent `add_dependency` fails for a different reason (e.g., a closed-ticket guard on the re-resolved target). In that case the original edge is permanently deleted while no replacement is written — a net data loss with no described recovery path.
findings.location: Approach section — 'Repair reuses the existing `add_dependency` and `unlink` write paths'; Testing — 'Failure: `--repair` on an edge whose re-resolution would create a cycle reports the edge as unrepairable'
scenarios: A mis-escalated edge's re-resolved target is closed. The unlink fires first, the add_dependency raises ValueError (closed-ticket guard). The original edge is gone; the replacement was never written. DATA LOSS RISK.
A mis-escalated edge's re-resolved pair passes cycle check but fails a future guard added after this plan is implemented. Same partial-failure shape.
findings.suggested_fix: Attempt `add_dependency` (dry-run or validate-only) before issuing the `unlink`; only if the re-resolved write would succeed does the repair proceed to unlink and then write. Alternatively, make the cycle-guard failure test exhaustive by also testing closed-ticket and other ValueError cases from `add_dependency`, and declare those equally 'unrepairable and left in place' — then the repair driver must attempt the write before the unlink.

findings.finding: Placing `link-audit` unconditionally in `_WRITES_FULL` (Scope) may trigger auto-init/reconverge side effects even in the default read-only invocation, contradicting AC #1 ('writes no events') and the Approach statement ('Default invocation is read-only').
scenarios: A developer runs `rebar link-audit` (no flags) in a repo that needs auto-init; reconverge writes events; the before/after event-count assertion in the test fails.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) register `link-audit` in a read-only bucket by default and only escalate to _WRITES_FULL when `--repair` is detected (as some other dual-mode commands do), or (b) add an explicit note in the plan that auto-init/reconverge is a no-op when the tracker is already current, so AC #1 is provably unaffected.
